title: Re-orienting without arguing during restlessness or confusion

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A dying person is restless, confused, frightened, or speaking from another reality; the witness wants to know whether to correct, comfort, call the nurse, or interpret it spiritually.
ordinary_language_queries: dying person confused what should I say
arguing with hallucinations at end of life

content_layers.observation_text: Public and professional sources describe restlessness, confusion, agitation, and delirium near death; professional material emphasizes assessment, causes, comfort, and medication decisions by clinicians.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK supports calm presence and orientation; PCNOW and NICE add clinical boundaries around terminal delirium and assessment. The record must separate delirium, visioning, and family meaning without collapsing them.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record is a hinge between symptom, relationship, and meaning. The archive should preserve the sentence said in the room while not deciding too quickly what kind of sentence it was.

what_this_is_not: not a diagnosis of delirium, dementia, psychosis, or spiritual experience
not a command to argue, correct, or validate every statement
not proof the person is afraid or not afraid
uncertainties: The boundary between delirium, dreams/visions, metaphor, and lucidity can be unclear.
New or severe agitation may require prompt clinical assessment.
Cultural and religious interpretations require participant-led framing.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should offer permission for calm, simple, non-argumentative presence while sending agitation, safety, or medication concerns to the care team.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect scripts that preserve dignity: orienting, naming safety, inviting family not to debate, and checking treatable causes.
language_notes: Do not use “hallucination” as the only frame.
Keep “seeing people” separate from “delirium” unless sourced and reviewed.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
